title: Apply to transfer a liquor licence (without previous licensee's consent)
summary: This page explains how to apply to transfer a liquor licence when the outgoing licensee has vacated the premises, been evicted, or has not agreed to the transfer.
intro:
If you are the premises owner or business owner and the outgoing licensee has vacated the premises, been evicted or hasn't agreed to transfer the licence, you may complete an 'owner in possession' transfer application.

Before applying, you must advise the outgoing licensee in writing or by email that you want a transfer and that they have 3 days to make a submission and provide evidence of this to Liquor & Gaming NSW.

Liquor & Gaming NSW will usually give you provisional approval within 10 business days so the business can continue operating. Confirmation of the transfer will take about 60 days if all relevant training has been completed.

For up-to-date liquor licence guidelines, resources and tools visit Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing.

If you have questions or feedback about liquor licensing contact Liquor & Gaming NSW.
what_you_need: Name and contact details of the person lodging the form
The intended transfer date (must be at least 10 business days after the application is received)
Representative's name and contact details (if applicable)
Proof of ownership (if you are the premises owner)
Details of the proposed licensee's (transferee's) industry experience and profile
A copy of the letter or email sent to the outgoing licensee advising them you want a transfer
Completed Data Monitoring Services direct debit request form – PDF (if operating gaming machines)
Copy of your NSW National Police Check certificate (must be less than 3 months old)
Copies of the 3 identity documents presented when you applied for the NSW National Police Check
Evidence of Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA) qualification
Evidence of Responsible Conduct of Gambling (RCG) qualification (if operating gaming machines)
Personal details of an appointed liquor approved manager
Transferee's current Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) company information report showing directors and shareholders

how_to_steps.text: Enter the details of the required licence.
Log in with your MyServiceNSW Account or create an account.
Follow the prompts to apply to transfer the licence.

faqs.q: How long does the transfer process take?
faqs.a: Liquor & Gaming NSW usually provides provisional approval within 10 business days, allowing the business to continue operating. Full confirmation of the transfer can take about 60 days if all relevant training is completed.

faqs.q: What should I do before applying for the transfer?
faqs.a: You must advise the outgoing licensee in writing or by email that you want a transfer, and they have 3 days to make a submission. You must provide evidence of this to Liquor & Gaming NSW.

faqs.q: Where can I find more information about liquor licensing?
faqs.a: For up-to-date guidelines, resources, and tools, visit the Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing page.
